A new word for what you do

Tutor vs Coach.

A tutor
Solves it while the child watches, then the child copies.
Jumps in with the answer the moment the child goes quiet.
Does most of the talking.
→→→
A Cuemath Coach
Makes the child do the thinking, and the explaining.
Holds the struggle, and keeps it productive.
Talks less. The child talks more.

About the classroom and the curriculum

The Cuemath Classroom.

Built for one-on-one math. Four things you'll learn to run.

Personalised learning
Every child on their own plan.

The child's MathFit report shapes what comes next.

1:1 attention
One coach. One child. Nowhere to hide.

You see the child's thinking as it happens.

Curriculum
K–12, concept first, and fun.

Games and puzzles before rules.

The live workbook
You both write on the same page.

Shared whiteboard, worksheets, a writing tablet on your side.

You'll be running all of this by Mock Session 1.

Class structure and the Talk Meter

What a Cuemath class looks like.

The same shape every time, so the child feels safe.

1
Warm-upIce-breaking, max 3 minutes.
2
ConceptThe child discovers the idea. You ask, they explain.
3
PracticeLive workbook. Hints, never answers.
4
Reflect and closeThe child says what they learned. You set the next step.
The Talk Meter

We measure who's talking.

Coach
Child

If you're doing most of the talking, the child isn't doing the thinking. Your mentor shows you your Talk Meter after every mock.

Things to keep in mind

How coaches make it through.

The ones who graduate keep a few ordinary habits.

Every day
⏰
Show up on time

Treat it like a paid class, because it leads to one.

Every day
📤
Submit on the day

Late work isn't reviewed late, it's reviewed less.

After feedback
🔧
Change one thing

Fix the note that matters most, visibly, next session.

Before you're stuck
🙋
Ask early

We love questions. Ask the moment you're unsure, not the night before a mock.

In every mock
⚡
Bring the vibe

A child feels your energy before they hear your words.

K–5
Basic fractions
3–8
Fractions, decimals, percentages and ratios, and how they relate
9–12
Quadratic equations and functions, including graphing
Know your topic cold. When in doubt, ask. We love questions.
